name: Techbot's Memory Core
summary: Techbot's Memory Core is the polarized central repository of Tinkmaster Overspark's mechanical assistant, Techbot. Recovered from the malfunctioning automaton within the corrupted depths of Gnomeregan, it contains the critical data Overspark hopes to use to reverse the machine's reversed, negatronic behavior.

sections.title: A Polarized Brain
sections.body: Before the catastrophe that forced the gnomes into exile, Techbot served Tinkmaster Overspark and his fellow inventors as an indispensable assistant, packed with gizmos and encyclopedic data. When Gnomeregan fell, an errant electrical discharge jolted the automaton, inverting its positronic brain into a hostile negatronic state. Driven mad by the reversal, Techbot now wanders the tainted halls of the city attacking anyone in sight. Recovering its memory core is Overspark's only hope for analyzing the malfunction and restoring his prized creation to its senses.

faq.answer: It is the primary data storage and computational center of Techbot, an automaton built by Tinkmaster Overspark. It holds the machine's knowledge and records the electrical disruption that corrupted its behavior during the fall of Gnomeregan.

aliases: where do i take techbots core
faq.answer: Tinkmaster Overspark seeks the core. Having taken refuge in Ironforge's Tinker Town alongside fellow exiled gnomes, he asks brave adventurers to venture into Gnomeregan, disable Techbot, and bring the core back so he can attempt repairs.

During the fall of Gnomeregan, a stray electrical spark jolted Techbot's positronic brain. The sudden surge polarized the mechanism, turning it negatronic and completely inverting the automaton's personality and protocols from helpful to violently frenzied.

aliases: where to get techbot memory core
faq.answer: The core is salvaged from Techbot itself, found roaming within the upper mechanical corridors and entrances of the fallen city of Gnomeregan in Dun Morogh.

angles.text: For gnomes, Techbot is another tragic casualty of Gnomeregan's fall, representing the loss of brilliant peacetime engineering to chaotic ruin.
Engineers can appreciate the bizarre hazards of positronic polarization, where a single electrical short can entirely invert an automaton's logic routines.
